title: Program Director, ReBuild Initiative
affiliation: Department of Urban Planning and Design
bio: Christine Gaspar is the Program Director of the ReBuild Initiative at the Harvard University Graduate School of Design, which aims to bring innovative design, theories, and tools into applied practice by civic leaders to rebuild, repair, and transform the urban fabric of cities in the U.S. and abroad. Christine is a recognized leader in community-engaged design practice, with a career focused on collaborating with marginalized communities, advocacy organizations, and local governments to shape the places where people live, build grassroots power, and strengthen democracy. Before joining the ReBuild team, Christine was the Executive Director of the Center for Urban Pedagogy (CUP), a New York-based nonprofit that co-creates educational materials and tools that help people access public services, legal rights, and political power. During her time there, CUP’s projects helped nail salon workers and street vendors expand their labor rights, rent stabilized tenants fight landlord harassment, and thousands of city residents participate in land-use decisions. She collaborated with New York City agencies to increase access to their affordable housing and public benefits. Christine was a founding steering committee member and led the creation of popular education materials and ballots for New York City’s participatory budgeting process.Prior to that, Christine was Assistant Director of the Gulf Coast Community Design Studio in Biloxi, Mississippi, where she provided architectural design and community planning services to low-income communities of color recovering from Hurricane Katrina. Earlier in her career, at the International City/County Management Association (ICMA), Christine conducted original research and authored influential policy papers on land use controls, and created a peer exchange program providing resources to local governments across the U.S. on redeveloping contaminated sites and facilitating sustainable growth. Christine’s work has been recognized with a Cooper Hewitt National Design Award for Institutional Achievement, the Curry Stone Design Prize, and the National Arts and Humanities Youth Program Award, and featured in contexts such as the Cooper-Hewitt Museum's National Design Triennial, PS-1, and the Venice Biennale. Christine’s research, in partnership with Liz Ogbu, on the role of grief and healing in community-engaged design practices has been awarded an AIA NY Arnold W. Brunner Grant for Architectural Research and Graham Foundation Research Grant.Christine has taught courses on design, civic engagement, and community planning at the School for Visual Arts, Parsons the New School for Design, the Pratt Institute, Mississippi State University, and Boston Architectural College, and has lectured about community-engaged design across the globe. She is a founding member and former Co-Chair of the Board of Design Futures Forum, and holds Masters degrees in Architecture and in Urban Planning from MIT, and a Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies from Brown University. Her work is driven by a belief that design can be a powerful tool, particularly when it’s used to support community-led visions for change.
